models.name: discussion_board_article_favorites
models.description:
Tracks user favorites and bookmarks for articles within the discussion platform.

Each record represents a specific article that a member has favorited or bookmarked for future reference. The system prevents duplicate favorites through a unique constraint combining member and article references. Favorites support optional categorization for user organization and include timestamps for creation, updates, and soft deletion tracking.

When a user removes a favorite, the record is soft-deleted (deleted_at set) rather than hard-deleted to maintain historical preferences and potential analytics. Favorites are user-specific and private to each member.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who created this favorite. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Article that was favorited. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: category
plainFields.description: Optional user-defined category for organizing favorites (e.g., "to-read", "research", "personal").

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional user notes about why this article was favorited or what to remember about it.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user favorited the article.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the favorite record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user removed the favorite, enabling soft deletion.

models.name: discussion_board_article_reactions
models.description:
Tracks user reactions (like, helpful, etc.) on articles for engagement analytics.

Each record represents a single reaction instance where a member expresses their sentiment toward an article. Reactions are simple positive feedback mechanisms that differ from comments or favorites. This table enables counting popular articles, identifying trending content, and understanding user engagement patterns.

The reaction system uses a defined set of reaction types to maintain consistency across the platform. Each member can only apply one of each reaction type per article to prevent spam and ensure authentic engagement metrics. {@link discussion_board_articles.id} is the target article being reacted to, and {@link discussion_board_members.id} identifies the member who created the reaction.

Reactions are independently managed entities that users can create and remove directly, separate from the article content itself. This enables features like reaction counters, user reaction history, and article popularity scoring.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Target article receiving the reaction. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who created the reaction. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

plainFields.name: reaction_type
plainFields.description: Type of reaction expressed (like, helpful, insightful, etc.). Uses predefined reaction types from system configuration.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reaction was created by the member.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reaction was last updated (if reaction type changed, though typically not).

models.name: discussion_board_article_metadata
models.description:
Additional metadata and extended attributes for articles beyond core content.

This table stores supplementary information that enhances article presentation and discovery, including SEO metadata for search engine optimization, reading time estimates for user convenience, and featured status flags for editorial curation. Unlike core article content which focuses on title, body, and section categorization, metadata provides auxiliary data that improves user experience and content management.

Each article can have exactly one metadata record, establishing a 1:1 relationship with the parent {@link discussion_board_articles} table. Metadata fields include SEO elements (meta title, description, keywords) for controlling how articles appear in search results, reading time calculations based on content length, and editorial flags for highlighting important content.

When articles are deleted, their associated metadata records are also removed through cascading deletion to maintain referential integrity.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. This establishes the 1:1 relationship between articles and their metadata records, ensuring each article has exactly one set of extended attributes.

plainFields.name: meta_title
plainFields.description: Custom title for SEO purposes, often shorter or more keyword-focused than the regular article title.

plainFields.name: meta_description
plainFields.description: SEO-optimized description that appears in search engine results and social media previews.

plainFields.name: meta_keywords
plainFields.description: Comma-separated keywords for search engine optimization and content categorization.

plainFields.name: reading_time_minutes
plainFields.description: Estimated reading time in minutes calculated based on article content length.

plainFields.name: is_featured
plainFields.description: Whether the article is marked as featured content for editorial highlighting and promotion.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the metadata record was originally created, typically matching the article creation time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the metadata record was last modified, tracking updates to SEO fields or featured status.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the metadata record was soft deleted, following the deletion of the parent article.

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Main comment table storing comment content, author association, article reference, and creation metadata.

Comments are single-level only with no nested replies, representing direct responses to articles. Each comment belongs to exactly one article and one author (member). Comments support editing history through {@link discussion_board_comment_snapshots} and soft deletion through {@link discussion_board_comment_deletions}. Users can edit and delete their own comments.

**Business Context:** Comments provide user discussion and feedback on articles. They are displayed in chronological order (oldest first) on article pages. Author profiles show their comment history, enabling cross-article search for user contributions.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Authoring member's {@link discussion_board_members.id}. Each comment has exactly one author who created it.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article's {@link discussion_board_articles.id}. Each comment belongs to exactly one article.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Comment text content. Supports Markdown formatting and inline media. Required for comment creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was initially created. Used for chronological ordering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last modified. Updates when content is edited.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When non-null, comment is considered deleted and hidden from public view.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of comment edits for audit trail and history tracking.

This table captures the complete state of a comment whenever it is edited, providing a historical record of changes. Each snapshot includes the comment content, author information, and related metadata at the time of the edit. These records support version comparison, audit compliance, and rollback capabilities.

Snapshots are created automatically whenever a comment is modified and form an append-only historical chain associated with the parent {@link discussion_board_comments.id}. Editors may optionally provide edit reasons for documentation purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment being snapshotted. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Comment text content at the time of snapshot creation. Captures the complete comment text including any formatting or markup.

plainFields.name: edit_reason
plainFields.description: Optional explanation provided by the editor for why the comment was modified. Used for documentation and transparency in edit history.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, marking the point-in-time capture of comment state.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_deletions
models.description:
Soft deletion records for comments, implementing polymorphic ownership pattern for different actor types (member, admin, superAdmin).

This table tracks when comments are soft-deleted, recording which actor performed the deletion, the reason, and audit timestamps. The actual comment deletion timestamp (deleted_at) is stored in the parent discussion_board_comments table, while this table provides actor-specific audit trail linking to subtype tables (discussion_board_comment_deletion_of_members, discussion_board_comment_deletion_of_admins, discussion_board_comment_deletion_of_super_admins).

Deleted comments are filtered out of public view via parent.deleted_at, while this record provides accountability and restoration capability for administrators. The polymorphic pattern ensures each actor type has its own subtype table with appropriate session and actor references.

Note: This table does NOT store the comment deletion timestamp itself - that's tracked in {@link discussion_board_comments.deleted_at}. This separation maintains proper normalization and prevents field duplication.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment that was deleted. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who performed the deletion (must match actual actor type: 'member', 'admin', or 'superAdmin'). Used to determine which subtype table contains the actor-specific details.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for deleting the comment. This can be provided by users when deleting their own comments or by administrators when removing content.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this deletion record was created, representing when the deletion audit trail was recorded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this deletion record was last updated. Typically updated if the deletion reason is modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at_deletion_record
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for this deletion record itself, allowing for cleanup of deletion records if needed. Null indicates active deletion record.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_activities
models.description:
Audit log of comment-related actions including editing, deletion, and admin moderation activities. Tracks all significant actions performed on comments for security, compliance, and debugging purposes. Each record represents a single action taken against a comment, capturing actor information, action type, and creation metadata. This table serves as the primary audit trail for comment lifecycle management with polymorphic actor ownership support.

{@link discussion_board_comments} for the comment being acted upon. Each activity can be associated with one actor through subtype tables for members, administrators, or super administrators.

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment that was acted upon. {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: Type of action performed on the comment. Common values: 'edit' (comment edited), 'delete' (comment deleted), 'undelete' (comment restored), 'admin_moderate' (administrative action), 'flag' (content flagged).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the action was recorded. Audit trails are append-only with immutable timestamps.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit record was last modified. For audit integrity tracking.

models.name: discussion_board_mv_article_comments
models.description:
Materialized view that pre-computes article comment statistics for fast querying.

Aggregates comment counts and latest comment timestamps for each article, optimizing queries that need to display comment statistics on article listing pages. This denormalized view is refreshed periodically to maintain performance while ensuring data consistency.

The view includes the article reference, comment count, and timestamp of the most recent comment, enabling fast sorting and filtering by comment activity without expensive JOIN operations on the live comments table.

{@link discussion_board_articles} for article details
{@link discussion_board_comments} for raw comment data

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced article for these comment statistics. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: total_comment_count
plainFields.description: Total number of comments on this article, including all published comments.

plainFields.name: latest_comment_timestamp
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent comment on this article for sorting by recent activity.

plainFields.name: refresh_timestamp
plainFields.description: When this materialized view was last refreshed to track data freshness.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_tags
models.description:
Junction table establishing many-to-many relationships between comments and tags for categorization and filtering.

Allows comments to be associated with multiple tags for better organization and searchability. Tags are optional metadata that help users filter discussions by topic or theme. This junction table enables the flexible tagging system while maintaining data integrity through foreign key constraints. The composite unique index ensures no duplicate tag associations for the same comment.

References: {@link discussion_board_comments.id} for comment associations, {@link discussion_board_tags.id} for tag definitions.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_id
foreignFields.description: Associated comment's {@link discussion_board_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was associated with the comment.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_deletion_of_members
models.description:
Subtype table for linking comment deletions performed by regular members (comment authors) to their member accounts and sessions.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for comment deletions, where deletions can be tracked by different actor types. Each comment deletion can be associated with exactly one member who performed the deletion, along with their session context for audit purposes.

This is a 1:1 subtype relationship with {@link discussion_board_comment_deletions}, ensuring each deletion record is linked to at most one member actor. The relationship provides full audit trail capability showing which member performed the deletion, from which session, and when.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_deletion_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent comment deletion record that was performed by this member. {@link discussion_board_comment_deletions.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member actor who performed the comment deletion. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member session active when the deletion was performed, providing audit context. {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this deletion association was created, matching the deletion time.

plainFields.name: updated_at

plainFields.name: deleted_at

models.name: discussion_board_comment_deletion_of_admins
models.description:
Subtype table that establishes audit trail linkages between comment deletion records performed by regular administrators and their administrative accounts and sessions.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for the comment deletion tracking system, specifically handling cases where regular administrators (not super administrators or regular members) delete comments. It provides accountability by associating each comment deletion with the specific administrator who performed the action and the session in which it occurred, enabling audit trails for administrative oversight.

When an administrator deletes a comment, this record is created to preserve the connection between the deletion event in {@link discussion_board_comment_deletions} and the administrator's identity via {@link discussion_board_admins.id} and their session via {@link discussion_board_admin_sessions.id}. This ensures compliance with platform governance requirements for tracking administrative actions.

The unique constraint on discussion_board_comment_deletion_id enforces a 1:1 relationship with parent deletion records, meaning each comment deletion can be linked to at most one administrator actor of this type.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_deletion_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent comment deletion record that this administrator performed. Each deletion can be linked to at most one administrator actor through the unique constraint. {@link discussion_board_comment_deletions.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the regular administrator account that performed the comment deletion. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_session_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the session in which the comment deletion was performed, establishing temporal and contextual linkage. {@link discussion_board_admin_sessions.id}.

models.name: discussion_board_comment_deletion_of_super_admins
models.description:
Subtype table linking super administrator-initiated comment deletions to super admin actor accounts and sessions.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for comment deletions, where comment_deletions references different actor types through subtype tables rather than nullable foreign keys. Each record represents a comment deletion performed by a super administrator, linking to their account and session at the time of deletion. The {@link discussion_board_comment_deletions.id} foreign key has a unique constraint to enforce 1:1 relationship with the main deletion entity.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_deletion_id

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: discussion_board_comment_activity_metadata
models.description:
Key-value storage for comment activity metadata that maintains First Normal Form (1NF) compliance by extracting structured metadata from JSON data.

This table stores detailed metadata for audit trail actions associated with comment activities, including old comment content before edits, specific fields changed during edits, deletion reasons, moderation details, and other structured metadata needed for audit purposes. Each metadata entry is linked to a specific comment activity record and stored as a normalized key-value pair.

{@link discussion_board_comment_activities.id} provides the audit context for these metadata entries, while this table enables structured querying of metadata that would otherwise be stored as unstructured JSON.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_activity_id
foreignFields.description: Parent comment activity record's {@link discussion_board_comment_activities.id}.

plainFields.name: updated_at

plainFields.name: value

models.name: discussion_board_comment_activity_by_members

Subtype table linking comment activities to member actors using polymorphic ownership pattern.

This table establishes a 1:1 relationship with the main comment activity table ({@link discussion_board_comment_activities}) and connects those activities to member user accounts and their sessions. It implements the polymorphic ownership pattern by storing the actor-specific metadata for member-performed comment activities such as editing, deletion, and moderation actions. This structure enables comprehensive audit trails of comment activities while maintaining proper actor separation.

Each record represents a specific comment activity performed by a member user, linking the activity to the member's identity and session context for accountability and audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_activity_id

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: discussion_board_comment_activity_by_admins
models.description:
Subtype table for comment activities performed by administrator actors, implementing polymorphic ownership pattern.

This table provides 1:1 relationship with the main {@link discussion_board_comment_activities} table while linking to administrator identity and session for comprehensive audit logging.

The table follows the subtype pattern for polymorphic actor ownership, allowing different actor types (member, admin, super admin) to have separate subtype tables while maintaining a clean separation of concerns. This supports administrator-specific audit requirements and permission tracking while preserving referential integrity.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_comment_activity_id

models.name: discussion_board_admin_requests
models.description:
Main table storing user applications to become administrators.

Each record represents a single request submitted by a member user seeking administrator privileges. The request includes a reason text explaining why the user wants to become an administrator and tracks the current status of the request (pending, approved, or rejected).

When a user submits an admin request, it remains in pending status until a super administrator reviews and makes a decision. Approved requests lead to administrator role assignment, while rejected requests are closed with the reason recorded in the decision table. Users can only have one active pending request at a time, enforced at application level.

All requests maintain audit trail with creation timestamps and support soft deletion for user withdrawal or administrative cleanup.

plainFields.name: status

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin request was submitted by the member user.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin request was last modified, including status changes or updates.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin request was soft deleted, either by user withdrawal or administrative cleanup. Null indicates active request.

models.name: discussion_board_admin_request_decisions
models.description:
Captures super administrator decisions on admin requests submitted by users seeking administrator privileges. Each record represents a final decision (approval or rejection) on an admin request, with timestamp and optional rejection justification. This table serves as the official governance record for administrator promotion decisions and provides audit trail for platform leadership transitions.

The decision records are maintained separately from the requests themselves to preserve immutable audit history. Super administrators exercise ultimate authority over administrator promotions as described in the governance transition mechanism. Each decision must reference exactly one admin request and the super administrator who made the decision, ensuring accountability and transparency in platform leadership changes.

foreignFields.name: admin_request_id

foreignFields.name: super_admin_id

plainFields.name: decision

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Optional reason text for rejection decisions. Only populated when decision is 'rejected', providing explanation for the denial of administrator promotion request. Required when rejecting to maintain transparency and guidance for future requests.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision was recorded. Captures the exact date and time the super administrator made the final decision on the admin request, serving as official decision timestamp for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision record was last updated. Tracks any modifications to the decision metadata, though decisions should be immutable after creation to preserve audit integrity.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision record was soft-deleted. Enables soft deletion capability while preserving audit trail integrity for historical compliance.

models.name: discussion_board_user_bans
models.description:
Records of user bans including reason, duration, banning administrator, and ban status.

This table tracks all user bans within the platform, supporting both temporary bans with expiration dates and permanent bans. Each ban includes the banned user reference, banning administrator, detailed reason text, and timing information. The table maintains the current status of each ban (active, expired, manually removed) and provides comprehensive audit trail for administrative oversight.

User bans prevent login access while preserving existing content visibility. Administrators can view the ban reason, duration, and banning details for each banned user. {@link discussion_board_members.id} references the banned user, while {@link discussion_board_admins.id} or {@link discussion_board_super_admins.id} references the administrator who performed the ban.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Banned member's identity. {@link discussion_board_members.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the ban action. {@link discussion_board_admins.id} for regular administrators or {@link discussion_board_super_admins.id} for super administrators.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation for why the user was banned, visible to administrators for review and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the ban: 'active' (currently preventing login), 'expired' (duration-based ban that has ended), 'removed' (manually un-banned by administrator).

plainFields.name: banned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban was initially imposed and became effective.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for temporary bans; null indicates a permanent ban with no automatic expiration.

plainFields.name: unbanned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when an active ban was manually removed by an administrator; null for bans that have not been manually lifted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ban record was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this ban record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for audit trail preservation; null indicates active record.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignments
models.description:
Tracks administrator role assignments and role transitions between member, administrator, and super administrator statuses.

Each assignment records the role change with previous and new roles, assignment type, reason, and temporal audit information. This table serves as an audit trail for platform governance decisions and supports tracking of administrator promotions, demotions, and initial assignments. It works in conjunction with {@link discussion_board_admin_requests} for request-based promotions and {@link discussion_board_audit_logs} for comprehensive administrative auditing.

Uses polymorphic ownership pattern with subtype tables for different actor relationships.

plainFields.name: old_role
plainFields.description: The user's role before this assignment. Possible values: 'member', 'admin', 'super_admin'. For initial administrator assignments from member, this would be 'member'.

plainFields.name: new_role
plainFields.description: The user's role after this assignment. Possible values: 'member', 'admin', 'super_admin'. This reflects the actual role change that occurred.

plainFields.name: assignment_type
plainFields.description: The type of assignment performed. Values: 'promotion' (moving to higher role), 'demotion' (moving to lower role), 'initial' (first-time assignment to admin), 'system' (system-initiated change).

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The rationale for the role change, similar to ban reasons. Should document why this assignment was made.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this assignment record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this assignment record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this assignment record was soft-deleted. Allows maintaining audit trail while removing from active queries.

models.name: discussion_board_audit_logs
models.description:
Comprehensive audit trail of all administrative actions performed by administrators and super administrators.

Records every administrative action including section management, content moderation, user banning, admin request decisions, and administrator role changes. Each entry tracks the actor who performed the action, the targeted entity, action specifics, and contextual details like IP address and user agent. Supports full audit capability for platform governance oversight, compliance tracking, and administrator performance evaluation.

Audit logs are immutable records that provide complete visibility into administrative decision-making processes. They enable super administrators to review regular administrator activities, ensure consistent application of platform policies, and maintain accountability for all governance actions. Each log entry preserves the context in which decisions were made, including timestamps, actor identification, and action rationale.

**Key Relationships:**
- References {@link discussion_board_admins} and {@link discussion_board_super_admins} as actors via polymorphic actor_type+actor_id
- References administrative targets via polymorphic target_type+target_id to entities like {@link discussion_board_sections}, {@link discussion_board_articles}, {@link discussion_board_comments}, {@link discussion_board_members}, etc.
- Linked to {@link discussion_board_administrative_histories} for comprehensive governance timeline

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrator who performed the action. Values: "admin" for regular administrators, "super_admin" for super administrators. Determines which actor table to reference via actor_id.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the administrator who performed the action. References either {@link discussion_board_admins.id} or {@link discussion_board_super_admins.id} based on actor_type.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity that was affected by the administrative action. Values: "section", "article", "comment", "user", "admin_request", "administrator_assignment", "user_ban". Determines which target table to reference via target_id.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the entity that was affected by the administrative action. References the appropriate target entity based on target_type.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed. Values: "create_section", "edit_section", "delete_section", "delete_article", "delete_comment", "ban_user", "unban_user", "approve_admin_request", "reject_admin_request", "promote_administrator", "demote_administrator". Categorizes the nature of the administrative action for querying and reporting.

plainFields.name: action_details
plainFields.description: Detailed description or rationale for the administrative action. Includes reason for banning, justification for content deletion, or explanation for admin request decision. Provides context for audit review and policy compliance assessment.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the administrative action was performed. Used for security auditing and identifying suspicious patterns across multiple administrators or locations.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string of the client used to perform the administrative action. Helps identify the device, browser, and operating system used for governance activities.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL or endpoint where the administrative action was triggered from. Provides technical context about the administrative interface used for the action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrative action was recorded. Represents when the governance decision was implemented in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit log entry was last updated. Typically matches created_at as audit logs are immutable, but preserved for consistency with temporal field patterns.

models.name: discussion_board_administrative_histories
models.description:
Comprehensive historical record of all administrative decisions, status changes, and role transitions for platform governance oversight.

This table serves as the audit trail for administrative actions across the platform, capturing changes to admin requests, user bans, administrator assignments, and other administrative states. Each record represents a point-in-time change in administrative status, allowing super administrators to review decision history, track role transitions, and monitor platform governance activities.

Key relationships include {@link discussion_board_admin_requests} for request status changes, {@link discussion_board_user_bans} for ban modifications, {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments} for role transitions, and {@link discussion_board_audit_logs} for action correlation.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who performed the action referenced in this historical record. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_request_id
foreignFields.description: Admin request that was subject to the status change, if applicable. Can be null for non-request-related actions. {@link discussion_board_admin_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: user_ban_id
foreignFields.description: User ban record that was subject to modification, if applicable. Can be null for non-ban-related actions. {@link discussion_board_user_bans.id}.

foreignFields.name: administrator_assignment_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator assignment record that was created or modified, if applicable. Can be null for non-assignment-related actions. {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments.id}.

foreignFields.name: audit_log_id
foreignFields.description: Corresponding audit log entry for this historical action, providing additional context. {@link discussion_board_audit_logs.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed (e.g., 'request_approval', 'request_rejection', 'user_ban', 'user_unban', 'role_promotion', 'role_demotion', 'status_change').

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity that was the target of this action (e.g., 'admin_request', 'user_ban', 'administrator', 'system_config').

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: UUID identifier of the target entity, used in conjunction with target_type to reference specific records.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the administrative action and its context for historical reference.

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description: Previous status/value before the administrative action was taken. Provides historical context for the change.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: New status/value after the administrative action was taken. Captures the outcome of the administrative decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this historical record was created. Represents when the administrative action was logged.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this historical record was last updated. Maintains data freshness for oversight activities.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_to_members
models.description:
Subtype table implementing polymorphic ownership pattern for administrator assignments where the assignment recipient is a member actor. Links administrator assignments to member accounts and their authentication sessions.

This table serves as a concrete subtype in the polymorphic ownership design, establishing the specific relationship between an administrator assignment and the member actor who receives the role assignment. Each record corresponds to exactly one administrator assignment instance and exactly one member actor, with the foreign key to member sessions providing audit trail context for when the assignment was created or modified.

Used by the system to track role transitions for community members who have been promoted to administrator status through the admin request approval process. Maintains 1:1 relationship with the parent {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments} table while linking to the specific actor type in the authentication system.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent administrator assignment record. {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member actor who receives the administrator assignment. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member session active when this assignment record was created or modified. Provides audit trail context. {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this assignment subtype record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this assignment subtype record was last modified.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_to_admins
models.description:
Subtype table linking administrator assignments to admin actors who receive role assignments.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for administrator assignments where the recipient is an admin actor. Each record establishes a 1:1 relationship between an administrator assignment and a specific admin account receiving administrative privileges. The table contains admin-specific metadata and session context for role assignment auditing and tracking.

Admin actors in this context are regular administrators who have already been promoted to administrative roles and are now receiving additional privilege assignments or role transitions. The 1:1 constraint ensures each administrator assignment references exactly one admin recipient while allowing the main assignment table to support multiple administrator assignment types through the polymorphic pattern.

{@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments.id} provides the core assignment metadata, while {@link discussion_board_admins.id} identifies the specific admin actor receiving the assignment.

foreignFields.name: administrator_assignment_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced administrator assignment's {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin actor receiving the role assignment's {@link discussion_board_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_session_id
foreignFields.description: Admin session context during assignment's {@link discussion_board_admin_sessions.id}.

plainFields.name: assigned_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator assignment was applied to the admin actor.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this subtype record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this subtype record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_to_super_admins
models.description:
Subtype table implementing polymorphic ownership for administrator assignments targeting super admin actors (those receiving role assignments).

This table establishes a 1:1 relationship between administrator assignments and super admin actors who are being assigned administrative roles or receiving promotions. It follows the polymorphic ownership pattern by separating actor-specific references into subtype tables, avoiding nullable actor foreign keys in the main assignment table.

Each record links a specific administrator assignment to exactly one super admin actor, maintaining referential integrity while supporting the complex role assignment system. The 1:1 constraint ensures each assignment has exactly one recipient super admin, and each super admin can receive multiple assignments over time.

{@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments} for the main assignment record.
{@link discussion_board_super_admins} for the super admin actor receiving the assignment.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the main administrator assignment record. {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_super_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the super admin actor receiving the assignment. {@link discussion_board_super_admins.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this subtype assignment relationship was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this subtype assignment relationship was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_by_members
models.description:
Subtype table implementing polymorphic ownership for administrator assignments performed by member actors.

This table establishes a 1:1 relationship with {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments} to track which member actor performed a specific administrator assignment action. It follows the polymorphic ownership pattern by providing subtype-specific references to member accounts and sessions for audit trail and accountability purposes.

Each record links a single administrator assignment to the member actor who executed it, along with their session context at the time of assignment. This enables audit trails, permission verification, and accountability tracking for administrative role assignment actions performed by regular members.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the main administrator assignment record. {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member actor who performed the assignment. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member session active during the assignment. {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this subtype assignment record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this subtype assignment record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_by_admins
models.description:
Subtype table implementing polymorphic ownership pattern for administrator assignments performed by admin actors.

Establishes a 1:1 relationship between {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments} and {@link discussion_board_admins}, tracking which admin actors performed administrator role assignments. This table enables the system to maintain audit trails and ownership information for administrative actions within the platform governance framework.

The table follows the subtype pattern to avoid multiple nullable foreign keys in the main assignment table, ensuring data integrity and supporting query optimization through explicit actor-type relationships.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the main administrator assignment record. This table implements a 1:1 relationship constraint ensuring each assignment performed by an admin actor has exactly one corresponding subtype record. {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the admin actor who performed the administrator assignment. Establishes the ownership relationship between the administrative action and the actor responsible. {@link discussion_board_admins.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this subtype relationship was created. Records when the admin actor was linked to the administrator assignment action.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this subtype relationship was last updated. Tracks modifications to the actor-assignment linkage.

models.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_by_super_admins
models.description:
Subtype table linking administrator assignments to super admin actors who performed the assignment.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for the "assigner" side of administrator assignments, specifically for super administrator actors. Each record establishes a 1:1 relationship between a main {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments} record and the super administrator actor (from {@link discussion_board_super_admins}) who performed the assignment, along with their session context (from {@link discussion_board_super_admin_sessions}) for comprehensive audit trail.

This table completes the administrator assignment tracking system, allowing all three actor types (members, admins, and super admins) to be properly tracked as assigners with appropriate session context and audit capabilities.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_administrator_assignment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the main administrator assignment record. This establishes the 1:1 relationship with {@link discussion_board_administrator_assignments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_super_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the super administrator actor who performed the assignment. Links to {@link discussion_board_super_admins.id} for identity verification.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_super_admin_session_id
foreignFields.description: Session context of the super administrator when performing the assignment. References {@link discussion_board_super_admin_sessions.id} for audit trail completeness.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this super admin assigner record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this super admin assigner record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_attachments
models.description:
Main attachment metadata table storing file information for articles.

Each attachment belongs to exactly one article and contains metadata about the uploaded file including filename, file type, size, and storage location. Attachments can be files or images, with image-specific metadata stored in {@link discussion_board_image_attachments}.

Attachments are managed through article operations - users upload files when creating or editing articles, and download files when viewing articles. The table tracks the lifecycle of file attachments including upload time and soft deletion status.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Parent article that this attachment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}

plainFields.name: filename
plainFields.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user. Preserves the original name for user recognition and download.

plainFields.name: filetype
plainFields.description: File extension or type identifier derived from the uploaded file (e.g., "pdf", "jpg", "docx").

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file for proper content-type headers during download (e.g., "application/pdf", "image/jpeg").

plainFields.name: size_bytes
plainFields.description: File size in bytes for storage tracking and download preparation.

plainFields.name: storage_path
plainFields.description: File system or cloud storage path where the actual file content is stored. Used by the storage service to retrieve file bytes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded and linked to the article.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment metadata was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was soft-deleted (nullable for active attachments).

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of attachment metadata for audit trail and version history.

Captures the complete state of an attachment at a specific moment in time, preserving the exact metadata values (filename, filetype, size, storage path, description) that existed at the snapshot timestamp. Used for compliance, rollback capabilities, and tracking changes to attachment metadata over time.

Each snapshot is immutable after creation and linked to its parent {@link discussion_board_attachments} entity. Snapshot content is denormalized from the parent to preserve historical accuracy.

**Design Rationale**: As a snapshot table, this denormalizes the parent attachment's state at capture time for audit purposes, rather than storing references to mutable parent fields.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Parent attachment being snapshotted. References {@link discussion_board_attachments.id}.

plainFields.name: captured_at
plainFields.description: Point-in-time when the attachment metadata was captured for this snapshot, representing the exact moment the parent's state was frozen.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this snapshot record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this snapshot record was last updated in the database.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: When this snapshot record was soft deleted. Allows preserving audit history while hiding from active queries.

models.name: discussion_board_image_attachments
models.description:
Image-specific metadata for attachment files including dimensions, alt text, and EXIF data reference.

This table stores specialized metadata for image-type attachments, providing dimensions, accessibility information via alt text, and references to EXIF data for camera and image properties. The table maintains a 1:1 relationship with {@link discussion_board_attachments.id} where each image attachment has exactly one set of image metadata.

Image dimensions are stored as integer values for width and height in pixels, supporting responsive display calculations. Alt text provides accessibility descriptions for screen readers and search engines. EXIF camera data is normalized into a separate child table to maintain database normalization while preserving detailed image metadata.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent image attachment record. {@link discussion_board_attachments.id}

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Image width in pixels. This is the horizontal dimension of the image file used for display calculations and responsive layouts.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Image height in pixels. This is the vertical dimension of the image file used for display calculations and responsive layouts.

plainFields.name: alt_text
plainFields.description: Accessibility alternative text describing the image content. Used by screen readers and displayed when images cannot be loaded.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image metadata record was created. Used for audit trail and version tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image metadata record was last updated. Used for tracking modifications to image properties.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this image metadata record was soft deleted, allowing for data recovery while hiding from normal queries.

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_downloads

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Downloaded attachment's {@link discussion_board_attachments.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the download was initiated by the user.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who performed the download. Values: 'guest', 'member', 'admin', 'super_admin'. Determines which actor subtype table to reference for the downloader identity.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the download request for security and geographic analytics.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: HTTP User-Agent header from the download request, identifying client browser/application.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP Referrer header indicating the page from which the download was initiated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this download record was soft deleted for compliance and audit trail purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_categories
models.description:
Predefined file type categories for organizing attachments into hierarchical groups such as documents, images, archives, and multimedia.

This table provides a taxonomy system for attachment classification, allowing administrators to create, manage, and organize attachment categories independently. Categories can be arranged hierarchically through parent-child relationships, with display ordering for consistent UI presentation. Activation status controls whether categories are available for use in the system.

Each category represents a logical grouping of attachment types that users can filter and browse by. The hierarchy supports nested categories like "Documents → PDFs" or "Images → Photos". Changes to categories are tracked through temporal fields, and soft delete preserves historical associations.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent category's {@link discussion_board_attachment_categories.id} for hierarchical organization. Null for top-level categories.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Display name of the category (e.g., "Documents", "Images", "Archives").

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description explaining the category's purpose and intended usage.

plainFields.name: order_index
plainFields.description: Display ordering position for consistent UI presentation, lower values appear first.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this category is currently available for use in the system. Inactive categories are preserved but not selectable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category was soft-deleted, preserving historical associations.

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_category_mappings
models.description:
Many-to-many relationship table connecting attachments to file type categories for organization.

Each row represents an assignment of a specific attachment to a specific file type category (e.g., document, image, archive). This enables flexible categorization where attachments can belong to multiple categories and categories can contain multiple attachments.

Used for organizing attachments by type for filtering, searching, and UI presentation. {@link discussion_board_attachments} can have multiple category assignments through this table, while {@link discussion_board_attachment_categories} can reference multiple attachments.

The junction table ensures proper normalization by separating categorization relationships from attachment and category metadata.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Associated attachment's {@link discussion_board_attachments.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_category_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned file type category's {@link discussion_board_attachment_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this category assignment was created.

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_thumbnails
models.description:
Generated thumbnail images with different sizes for fast preview loading.

This table stores resized versions of attachments (primarily images) optimized for quick display in user interfaces. Each attachment can have multiple thumbnail versions at different sizes (e.g., small, medium, large). Thumbnails are generated on upload and cached to improve page load performance.

Key relationships:
- Each thumbnail belongs to exactly one parent attachment ({@link discussion_board_attachments})
- The main attachment table tracks the original file while this table stores derivative versions
- Thumbnails are managed automatically and not directly by users

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Parent attachment that this thumbnail is derived from. {@link discussion_board_attachments.id}

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Width of the thumbnail image in pixels.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Height of the thumbnail image in pixels.

plainFields.name: size_category
plainFields.description: Standard size category for the thumbnail (e.g., 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'extra_large'). Used for consistent thumbnail generation across the platform.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the thumbnail file in bytes.

plainFields.name: file_path
plainFields.description: Storage path where the thumbnail file is saved in the file system or cloud storage.

plainFields.name: content_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the thumbnail image (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp').

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this thumbnail was generated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this thumbnail record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this thumbnail was soft-deleted. Null indicates active thumbnail.

models.name: discussion_board_image_attachment_exif_data
models.description:
Stores camera and image EXIF metadata extracted from image attachments. Contains detailed photographic information including camera manufacturer, model, lens specifications, exposure settings, flash configuration, and GPS coordinates when available.

This table provides technical metadata that enriches image attachments with professional camera data, enabling advanced image analysis and organization. EXIF data is typically extracted during image upload and provides valuable context about image creation conditions.

Each record corresponds to exactly one image attachment in {@link discussion_board_image_attachments}. The relationship is 1:1 since each image attachment has a single set of EXIF metadata. The metadata is primarily read-only once extracted, though technical corrections may be applied if needed.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_image_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent image attachment's {@link discussion_board_image_attachments.id}. This establishes a 1:1 relationship where each image attachment has exactly one EXIF metadata record.

plainFields.name: camera_make
plainFields.description: Manufacturer of the camera that captured the image (e.g., Canon, Nikon, Sony).

plainFields.name: camera_model
plainFields.description: Specific model of the camera used to capture the image (e.g., EOS R5, D850, α7 III).

plainFields.name: lens_model
plainFields.description: Lens model information including focal length and aperture range when available.

plainFields.name: exposure_time
plainFields.description: Shutter speed or exposure time expressed as a fraction (e.g., '1/125', '1/60').

plainFields.name: f_number
plainFields.description: Aperture f-number setting (e.g., 2.8, 4.0, 5.6).

plainFields.name: iso_speed
plainFields.description: ISO sensitivity setting used for the exposure.

plainFields.name: focal_length
plainFields.description: Focal length in millimeters used for the shot.

plainFields.name: flash_fired
plainFields.description: Whether flash was fired during the exposure.

plainFields.name: metering_mode
plainFields.description: Metering mode used for exposure calculation (e.g., Center-weighted, Spot, Evaluative).

plainFields.name: white_balance
plainFields.description: White balance setting (e.g., Auto, Daylight, Cloudy, Tungsten).

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_download_guests
models.description:
Subtype table linking attachment download records to guest actors for polymorphic ownership.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for download references, allowing guest actors (temporary anonymous users) to be associated with download activities. Each record establishes a 1:1 relationship between an attachment download record and a guest actor, along with the guest session that initiated the download. This enables guest-specific analytics and access control while maintaining the separation between actor types through subtype tables.

The table references the parent {@link discussion_board_attachment_downloads}, the associated {@link discussion_board_guests} actor, and the {@link discussion_board_guest_sessions} for session context. Downloads by guests are tracked for analytics and security monitoring of anonymous access to attachment files.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_download_id

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_guest_id
foreignFields.description: The guest actor who performed the download. References the temporary anonymous user account. {@link discussion_board_guests.id}.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_guest_session_id
foreignFields.description: The guest session context when the download was initiated. Provides session metadata for audit purposes. {@link discussion_board_guest_sessions.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest download reference was created. Records when the polymorphic association was established.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this guest download reference was last updated. Tracks any modifications to the association metadata.

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_download_members
models.description:
Subtype table implementing polymorphic ownership for member actor attachment downloads.

Links individual download records from {@link discussion_board_attachment_downloads} to specific member actors from {@link discussion_board_members}. This table enables type-safe polymorphic relationships where attachment downloads can be owned by different actor types (guests, members, admins, super admins) through separate subtype tables, avoiding the anti-pattern of multiple nullable foreign keys.

Each record establishes a 1:1 relationship: one download belongs to exactly one member actor through this subtype. The main download record tracks generic download metadata while this subtype adds actor-specific context. When querying downloads by member actors, join through this table to retrieve download activity with proper actor typing.

foreignFields.description: Reference to the member actor who performed the download. {@link discussion_board_members.id}

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Session context when the download occurred. {@link discussion_board_member_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: created_at

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this subtype record was last updated.

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_download_admins
models.description:
Subtype table linking download records to admin actors for polymorphic ownership.

This table establishes the specific relationship between file download activities and admin actor accounts. It is part of a polymorphic ownership pattern where the main {@link discussion_board_attachment_downloads} table tracks download activities generically, while subtype tables like this one link downloads to specific actor types.

The 1:1 relationship is enforced through a unique constraint on the download foreign key, ensuring each download record can be associated with exactly one actor type reference. This design supports clean separation of concerns while maintaining referential integrity across the polymorphic ownership system.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_attachment_download_id

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: discussion_board_attachment_download_super_admins
models.description:
Subtype table linking download records to super admin actors for polymorphic ownership.

This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern where attachment download records can reference different actor types. Each record establishes a 1:1 relationship between a download event and a super admin actor who performed the download. The table ensures referential integrity while maintaining separation of actor types.

Records in this table are created when a super admin downloads an attachment, linking the download activity to their administrative account for audit trails and access tracking. This approach avoids nullable foreign keys in the main download table and provides clean actor type separation.
